title: Outpatient Aftercare and the Step-Down Day on Inpatient Closures, Referrals and Authorizations
content:
Outpatient aftercare decides the step-down day when the cancellation of an approved Skilled Nursing Facility Authorization or Inpatient Mental Health Authorization covered under TRICARE Prime is confirmed under **Referrals and Authorizations**.

## Source records

- The last covered day: the latest use entry in the authorization's unit history (by service date) covers its service date for the days it posted, so its last covered day is that service date plus those days, less one day.
- The patient's most recent outpatient behavioral health visit, from the patient's TRICARE Prime claim lines (the latest individual outpatient behavioral health line by service date).
- Whether there is a readmission inside the span: the patient's most recent emergency department visit on the TRICARE Prime claim lines is dated after the last covered day and on or before the authorization's last span day.

## Determination

1. Where the patient's most recent outpatient behavioral health visit falls after the last covered day and within seven days of it, aftercare picked the patient up, and **1 day is added back** to the release.
2. Where it falls more than seven days after the last covered day and there is a readmission inside the span (the patient's most recent emergency department visit is dated after the last covered day and on or before the span's last day), **1 more day is held** for a step-down to partial hospitalization.
3. Otherwise nothing changes.

## Illustrations (hypothetical; last covered day 7 March, last span day 15 March)

| Most recent outpatient visit | Most recent emergency visit | Effect on the release |
|---|---|---|
| 14 March (7 days after) | any | 1 day added back |
| 15 March (8 days after) | 10 March | 1 day held |
| 15 March (8 days after) | 20 March, after the span | none |
| 15 March (8 days after) | 5 March, not after the last covered day | none |
| 7 March, the last covered day itself | any | none |
